_comment: Shared fixture for WHEN A DOSE HAPPENED in the medication's own local time — which
DAY it belongs to, and which time-of-day SLOT within that day.
Sibling of schedule-test-vectors.json and it exists for the same reason: the same
logic is implemented twice (TypeScript in web/src/lib/design/slots.ts, Kotlin in the
alarm core when it tints its ground by dose time and when it groups a day), and two
implementations of one rule drift. calculateNextReminder already proved that — its two
JS copies were described as 'lockstep' and had silently diverged on empty input.
Share the TESTS, not the code. Both engines must pass every vector below.
Three decisions encoded here, all deliberate:
1. MORNING STARTS AT HOUR 0, not 05:00. A 03:00 dose is real in this app
(night-shift workers, strict-interval antibiotics). Calling 03:00 'morning' is
a small labelling inaccuracy; a dose landing in NO slot and vanishing off the
rail would be a bug. Correctness over label aesthetics.
2. SLOTTING USES THE MEDICATION'S TIMEZONE, never the device's. A dose set for
08:00 Asia/Kolkata is a morning dose even when the phone is in London.
Getting this wrong mistints a travelling patient's entire day.
3. A DOSE'S DAY IS ALSO THE MEDICATION'S DATE, never the UTC date and never the
viewer's. For IST (UTC+5:30) those disagree for EVERY dose between 00:00 and
05:29 local — which is exactly where this app's 01:00-03:00 doses live. The
`utcDay` field below is recorded on the cross-day vectors to show what the
naive implementation would have produced; nothing asserts against it.
Boundaries: morning [00:00-10:59], midday [11:00-15:59], evening [16:00-20:59],
night [21:00-23:59]. Boundaries are INCLUSIVE at the start of each slot.
expectedSlot is one of: morning | midday | evening | night, or null meaning
'engine-local, do not assert' (the zone is absent or invalid, so the answer depends
on where the test runs).
expectedDay is YYYY-MM-DD, or null meaning 'the engine must return no day at all'
(an unparseable instant has no honest day). A vector that OMITS expectedDay is one
the day rule cannot assert — same engine-local reason as a null expectedSlot.
